Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the RetailWave Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask questions after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to RetailWave Inc.'s Q3 2023 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Jenkins, CEO; Mike Rivera, CFO; Lisa Chen, COO; David Patel, CMO; Elena Vasquez, CTO; and Raj Singh, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, CEO of RetailWave Inc.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust promotional strategies that boosted sales while maintaining profitability discipline, alongside impressive revenue acceleration. We saw significant growth in key metrics like gross merchandise value and active buyers.

Our focus remains on scaling our marketplace flywheel through AI-enhanced personalization and omnichannel expansion. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our WavePrime loyalty program enhancements, which we believe will significantly drive repeat purchases and customer lifetime value.

We are investing heavily in supply chain automation and regional localization to capture emerging market share.

We are focused on improving operational efficiencies across fulfillment and marketing spend.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth regions like APAC and LATAM.

Finally, we are committed to leveraging data science for conversion optimization and sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Rivera, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Our Q3 revenue was $1.47 billion, an increase of 22% year-over-year and 10% quarter-over-quarter, comfortably exceeding our guidance range. This strong top-line momentum underscores the resilience of our e-commerce platform in a dynamic macro environment. Gross margin was 33.8%, reflecting some pressure from promotions but offset by volume leverage. Operating expenses were $450 million, representing 30.6% of revenue, with meaningful improvements in efficiency.

Before diving deeper into forward guidance, let me unpack the key driver behind these results: the impact of our promotional activities on sales and profitability. In this hyper-competitive e-commerce space—think Amazon's Prime Day or Alibaba's Singles' Day—promotions drive growth but demand precision to safeguard margins. We've refined our approach with data science and regional tailoring, and the outcomes are clear.

Promotional activities drove 38% of our total GMV, up from 32% YoY, powering that 22% net sales growth. Flash sales and site-wide discounts, modeled after Black Friday but timed mid-quarter, lifted units sold 45% during those windows, with average order value steady at $85 through bundling. Electronics saw the biggest surge: promo GMV up 58% YoY, grabbing share from competitors like Best Buy online amid softer demand.

Conversion rates rose 12% to 4.2% during promos, thanks to our AI personalization engine on Adobe Experience Cloud, dynamically recommending deals and boosting add-to-cart by 28%. Mobile promo traffic was 62% of sessions, riding the TikTok Shop and Instagram Shopping wave with video ads offering 20-30% off codes sparking impulse buys in apparel and beauty.

Regionally, North America at 55% of GMV grew 26% YoY, with WavePrime—now 18 million subscribers—adding 15% incremental GMV through early access perks. Europe, 28% of GMV, rose 19% despite VAT hurdles on discounts; we shifted to localized flash sales with Amazon.de and Zalando partners, focusing on free shipping. APAC, 17% of GMV, jumped 35% via Singles' Day prep on Tmall and 11.11 events, managing inventory turns at 8.2x versus the 6.5x industry average.

On profitability, gross margins dipped 210 basis points to 33.8% from deeper discounts averaging 24%, especially clearing home goods inventory. Adjusted EBITDA margins compressed to 11.2% from 12.8%, but contribution margins per order improved 8% to $22.50 as promo traffic cut CAC 14% to $18 via SEO uplift. ROAS on Google Shopping and Meta reached 5.2x, aided by our ML bid optimizer prioritizing high-LTV segments. We sidestepped promo fatigue like Wayfair's, with post-promo repeat rates at 42% versus 35% industry, preserving CLTV at $450.

We've introduced the Prometheus pricing engine on AWS SageMaker for real-time elasticity modeling, testing 1,200 variants weekly on 50 SKUs. In apparel, tiered discounts—15% on first item, 30% on third—grew basket size 18% without margin hits. Promo attribution via incrementality tests shows 65% incremental sales.

For Q4, we guide $1.65-1.72 billion in sales, promos at 42% of GMV, margins stabilizing at 34-35% through targeted WavePrime stacks for 20% GMV uplift and 3.5x LTV/CAC; APAC gamified promos with Shopee; EU VAT-compliant vouchers on sustainability bundles; RFID-synced inventory for 95% fill rates; and capping promos at 12% of days to protect hero SKUs, as 68% of Gen Z value perception drives loyalty.

Turning to revenue growth specifics, this 22% YoY and 10% QoQ beat our guide by wide margins, with GMV up 24% to around $4.2 billion and take rates steady. TTM revenue trajectory supports mid-20s full-year growth ahead of consensus. YoY was powered by 25% active buyer ramp, offset slightly by mix. Constant currency was 23%, muting FX headwinds from euro and real. QoQ accelerated from prior summer softness, thanks to quick-commerce groceries up 40%.

We outperformed on buyer growth, take rates up modestly via ads and fulfillment fees, and hedging. Marketplace revenue, 72% of total, grew 25%, led by third-party sellers at 65% GMV. Advertising jumped 30% to $220 million or 15% of revenue, with SphereSuggest GenAI boosting CTR 18% and conversions 14%. First-party retail grew 15% on private labels.

North America 14% growth to $815 million, Europe 22% to $410 million on UK fulfillment and livestreams averaging 2.5 million viewers. APAC 28%, LATAM 25% on Pix payments. Tech backbone processed orders at 99.9% on-time, drones shaving last-mile times, NPS up 8 points. CAC fell 11% to $28, payback at 4 months.

We're raising full-year guidance to $6.4-6.6 billion, 20-23% growth. Q4 $1.65-1.72 billion.

On operating expenses, we hit $450 million or 30.6% of sales, down 410 bps YoY and 120 bps QoQ, expanding adjusted operating margin to 9.2% from 5.8%. Fulfillment at $180 million or 12.2%, down 150 bps, from micro-fulfillment centers cutting miles 22%, 150 robotic systems boosting throughput 35%, labor down 18%. APAC partnerships lowered last-mile 12%, EMEA algorithms cut failed deliveries 9%. CPAC to $4.82, 14% better.

Marketing $110 million or 7.5%, flat YoY but ROAS to 4.8x, shifting to performance channels, CAC to $22. Pruned low-ROI SEM, leaned into groceries LTV/CAC over 5:1, influencers 6.2x ROAS.

Tech/content $65 million or 4.4%, steady, funding GenAI recs up 19% acceptance, AOV +7%. G&A $65 million, headcount down 2%, $50 million synergies from acquisition.

Op-ex to GMV down 320 bps to 26.5%, inventory turns 8.2x. Sustainability cut emissions 15%, $30 million incentives. Expect 100-200 bps more leverage H2.

Our net income for the quarter was $120 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended with $850 million in cash and equivalents. Reaffirming full-year guidance with upside.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa Chen to discuss operations.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Mike. Operationally, we focused on supply chain optimization and last-mile innovation. Our shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs per order fell to $7.82, a 15% YoY drop from $9.20 and 4% QoQ from $8.15—our lowest ever. TTM down 22% from $10.04, beating Shopify peers.

This stems from our Fulfillment Excellence Program. Labor down 18% to $3.28 via 1,200 robots boosting picks to 350/hour, headcount cut 22%. Inbound/packaging $1.45, ML predictions 97% accurate. Outbound $2.97, dynamic bidding saved $0.45/package, drones sub-$2 last-mile.

North America $7.45, mega-DC 1.2 million units daily. Europe $8.65, micro-fulfs cut duties 24%. APAC $7.15, same-day 40%. Each $1 saved adds $180 million EBITDA on 180 million orders, NPS to 78, LTV +14%.

CapEx $450 million for GenAI orchestration 10-12% more cuts, EV fleets, BOPIS shaving $1.20/order.

Now I'll turn it over to David Patel.

David Patel:
Thanks, Lisa. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from performance max on Google/Meta and TikTok Shop UGC. Customer acquisition costs were $38.20 blended, down 12% YoY and 7% QoQ from $41.10—sixth straight quarter of gains, below $52 industry average. Apparel $32.50, electronics $48.70.

$285 million spend up 4% YoY but 28% more customers, ROAS 4.8x from 4.2x, payback 4.2 months versus 6-8 norm.

Paid search 32% spend, CAC $29.80, ROAS 6.2x, Performance Max +15% conversions. Social 45%, CAC $42.10, ROAS 4.1x, TikTok sub-$35. Affiliates 12%, $25.40 CAC, 7.9x ROAS. Email/SMS $10 CAC, 12x+ ROAS.

AI bid opt on Vertex AI cut Meta 11%, unified graph +27% lookalikes, geo-tests 68% incremental. Marketing scalability score 142 from 118.

North America $36.50 CAC, ShopFast Express. EMEA $44.20, Pinterest strong. APAC $51.80, Lazada 4.3x.

LTV $285, 7.5:1 ratio. Guide $37-39 CAC, 5.0x+ ROAS.

Now I'll turn it over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, David. On the technology front, we've been focused on mobile optimization and GenAI personalization. Our website uptime was 99.9%. Mobile app usage increased by 28%, with 5.2 million downloads, 18% YoY MAU to 52 million (68% of users), DAU 16.8 million, 32% DAU/MAU.

Day 1 retention 52%, D7 38%, D30 22%. North America 28 million MAU, AR try-on. APAC 14 million, UPI +25% sessions. Europe 6.2 million.

App conversion 4.8%, up 15% YoY, versus 2.9% web. Grocery 7.2%, ARPU $42 +19%. SwiftCart 2.0 cut abandonment 37%, GenAI chat +18%, load times 1.2s.

72% GMV from app. Guide Q4 downloads +25%, MAU +16%, conversions +12%.

Now I'll turn it over to Raj Singh.

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Elena. Data science is a key focus. We've seen a 15% improvement in conversion rates from NovaRecs 2.0. Active buyers hit 152 million, 28% YoY, 8% QoQ, beating guide.

Added 42 million net new, 35% YoY. Paid CAC $28, ROAS 4.8x. Organic +32%, BNPL +12 million, Shopify 5 million. APAC 18 million, North America 10 million.

Retention 87% 12-month cohort, D90 62%, 4.2 orders/buyer, AOV $68 +12%. AI recs +28% repeats, NovaPrime 18%, Buyer Circles 15% higher.

LTV/CAC 3.8x. Guide Q4 25-27% growth, 86%+ retention.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Jamie Lee with Goldman Sachs.

Jamie Lee:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Mike, can you expand on how promotions impacted margins and your Q4 outlook there?

Mike Rivera:
Thanks, Jamie. As I detailed, promos drove 38% of GMV but dipped gross margins 210 bps due to 24% discount depth. We offset with volume, CAC cuts, 5.2x ROAS, and 65% incremental lift. Q4 bakes 42% promo GMV but 34-35% margins via tiers, localization, inventory sync, and frequency caps—positioning for outperformance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Morgan Stanley.

Rachel Kim:
Great, thanks. Mike, on revenue—how sustainable is the QoQ acceleration, and regional details?

Mike Rivera:
Rachel, the 10% QoQ beat models on quick-commerce and ads. Sustainable via flywheel: North America 14% on staples, Europe 22% livestreams, APAC/LATAM 28%/25% on partnerships. Raised FY guide reflects this.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Patel with JPMorgan.

Tom Patel:
Lisa, fulfillment cost per order trends—any risks to further declines?

Lisa Chen:
Tom, $7.82 is inflection from robots, bidding, drones. Regional: NA best, APAC lowest. CapEx for GenAI, EVs, BOPIS ensures 10-12% more cuts, resilient to disruptions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Wong with Barclays.

Sarah Wong:
David, impressive CAC compression—what's driving social efficiency post-ATT?

David Patel:
Sarah, server-side tagging, TikTok UGC at sub-$35 CAC, ML bids cut 11%, unified graph +27%. ROAS 4.1x social, scaling CTV pilots. LTV synergies keep payback short.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Evans with Bank of America.

Chris Evans:
Elena, mobile app—how are you sustaining DAU/MAU above peers?

Elena Vasquez:
Chris, 32% ratio from personalized pushes 3.2x opens, SwiftCart -37% abandonment, GenAI chat +18%. 72% GMV app-sourced, app-only bundles targeting 5.5% conversions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Grant with Citi.

Lisa Grant:
Raj, active buyer growth—retention details and cohort trends?

Raj Singh:
Lisa, 152 million actives, 42 million new at $28 CAC. Retention 87% cohort, NovaPrime halves churn, Circles viral. 2023 cohort 82% year 2, 3.8x LTV/CAC.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Sarah Jenkins for closing remarks.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
